name: mt63
label: MT63-1000L (robust HF data / EmComm)
description: MT63 is a highly robust HF data mode — 64 parallel DBPSK tones with heavy interleaving and FEC, designed to punch through fading, interference and poor copy where RTTY/PSK fail. The 1000L variant (1 kHz wide, long interleave) is the EmComm/MARS workhorse for net traffic and bulletins. On the waterfall it's an unmistakable solid rectangular block of energy. Decoded text streams under decoder::fldigi (vendored fldigi MT63 core). Long interleave means it takes several seconds to start producing text and to flush at the end — that latency is the price of its robustness. Tune so the 1 kHz block is centred ~1500 Hz in the USB audio (dial ≈ centre − 1.5 kHz). Audio is teed alongside so you can listen.
ai_notes: MT63-1000L (64-tone DBPSK, 1 kHz, long interleave; vendored fldigi mt63 core). EmComm/MARS/net mode — no fixed amateur watering hole; commonly 14.109 / 7.073 / 3.588 MHz on nets, plus MARS channels. Tune dial ≈ centre − 1500 Hz. Several-second decode latency by design (interleaver fill). Output: `tail decoder --category fldigi`. Variants via Mt63Demod `mode`: mt63-500S/L, mt63-1000S/L, mt63-2000S/L.
